title: Bias in the Tails: How Name-conditioned Evaluative Framing in Resume Summaries Destabilizes LLM-based Hiring
abstract: arXiv:2604.19984v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Research has documented LLMs' name-based bias in hiring and salary recommendations. In this paper, we instead consider a setting where LLMs generate candidate summaries for downstream assessment. In a large-scale controlled study, we analyze nearly one million resume summaries produced by 4 models under systematic race-gender name perturbations, using synthetic resumes and real-world job postings. By decomposing each summary into resume-grounded factual content and evaluative framing, we find that factual content remains largely stable, while evaluative language exhibits subtle name-conditioned variation concentrated in the extremes of the distribution, especially in open-source models. Our hiring simulation demonstrates how evaluative summary transforms directional harm into symmetric instability that might evade conventional fairness audit, highlighting a potential pathway for LLM-to-LLM automation bias.

translated_title: 尾部偏差：简历摘要中基于姓名条件的评价性框架如何破坏基于大语言模型的招聘稳定性
translated_abstract: 已有研究记录了大语言模型在招聘和薪资推荐中基于姓名的偏见。在本文中，我们转而考虑LLM为下游评估生成候选人摘要的场景。在一项大规模对照研究中，我们使用合成简历和真实职位发布，分析了4个模型在系统性种族-性别姓名扰动下生成的近百万份简历摘要。通过将每份摘要分解为基于简历的事实内容和评价性框架，我们发现事实内容基本保持稳定，而评价性语言则表现出细微的基于姓名条件的变化，这种变化集中在分布的极端部分，在开源模型中尤为明显。我们的招聘模拟展示了评价性摘要如何将方向性伤害转化为对称的不稳定性，从而可能规避传统的公平性审计，揭示了LLM到LLM自动化偏见的一条潜在路径。
tldr: 该研究通过分析近百万份LLM生成的简历摘要，首次揭示基于姓名的偏见并非体现在事实内容上，而是集中于评价性语言的分布尾部，将方向性歧视转化为可规避传统公平审计的对称不稳定性。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that name-based bias in LLM-generated resume summaries manifests not in factual content but in evaluative language concentrated at distributional tails, transforming directional harm into symmetric instability that evades conventional fairness audits.
